answers.a: The Manila International Research Conference 2026 (MIRC 2026) is a hybrid international academic conference that brings together researchers, academicians, practitioners, policymakers and students from diverse disciplines. It focuses on the role of artificial intelligence, sustainability and innovation in building resilient, inclusive and future‑ready communities. The main conference takes place on 29‑30 September 2026 at the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) in Intramuros, Manila.

The conference runs from 27 to 30 September 2026.  
- 27 Sept 2026: Hospitality & Tourism sub‑conference at DLSU‑CSB.  
- 29–30 Sept 2026: Main conference at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM).
The conference takes place at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM), located at Gen. Luna Cor. Muralla Streets, Intramuros, Manila, Philippines 1002.

answers.q: What can I see in Intramuros?
answers.a:
You can visit several heritage sights within walking distance of the PLM venue:
- Memorare — Manila 1945 (Free, ~10 min walk, 6 min from venue) – a 1995 memorial sculpture honoring the civilians killed in the Battle of Manila.  
- Museo de Intramuros (₱200, ₱160 for students/seniors/PWD, ~1 hr visit, 6 min walk) – the Intramuros Administration’s collection of colonial religious art inside the rebuilt San Ignacio Church.  
- Plaza México (Free, ~15 min walk) – a square commemorating the historic Manila–Acapulco galleon trade.  
- Plazuela de Santa Isabel (Free, ~10 min walk) – a small square that holds the Memorare monument, on the former site of one of Asia’s oldest girls’ schools.  
- San Agustin Church (Free, ~30 min visit, 3 min walk) – the oldest stone church in the Philippines, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a trompe‑l’œil ceiling.  
- Santa Lucia Barracks Ruins (Free, ~15 min walk) – the remaining foundations of Spanish infantry barracks, left unreconstructed as a reminder of the 1945 destruction.
